name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 19, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the
City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:01 p.m.,
on September 19, 2011, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 16, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Reardon
  Mayor Pro Tem Ury
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  Council Member Kelley

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  W. Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Reardon

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with the City’s Real Property Negotiators Pursuant to Government
  Code Section 54956.8. Real property Denoted as Assessor’s Parcel No. 784-291-01
  with a Common Street Address of 24701 San Doval, Mission Viejo, California,
  Commonly Known as O’Neill Elementary School Owned by Saddleback Valley

City Council Minutes  1  September 19, 2011
   Unified School District The Negotiating Parties are: City of Mission Viejo; Dennis
  Wilberg, City Manager, Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager, Charles Wilson,
  Director of Community Development, and William Curley, III, City Attorney.
  Owner Negotiators are: Saddleback Valley Unified School District, Clint Harwick,
  Superintendent. Under Negotiation will be the Price and Terms of a Lease-Hold
  Interest in the Real Property.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member
Kelley was absent.)

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council provided direction to staff but there
was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Musical Presentation by Saxophonist Ricky Sims

  Saxophonist Ricky Sims preformed for the City Council and audience.

P2.  Proclaim October 5, 2011 to Be "International Walk to School Day" in the City of
  Mission Viejo

  Mayor Leckness presented the proclamation to Community Services Manager Steve Bell.

P3.  3rd Annual Readers’ Festival

  Stephanie Tanton, Director of Library Services, highlighted the authors attending and the
  events planned for the 3rd Annual Readers’ Festival on October 1, 2011.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: reminded the City Council that on July 5, 2011, he cautioned the City
Council and Special Counsel Celeste Brady that they were about to adopt a resolution that
contained false statements and he expressed opposition to item 20 on the agenda tonight.

Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.: thanked Mayor Leckness for a great time on the tour of the Oso Creek
Trail this afternoon.

City Council Minutes  2  September 19, 2011
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 11, 12, 15, 17, 19, and 20 were removed from the Consent Calendar for
separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to approve the Consent
Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Kelley

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

5.  Check Register dated September 2, 2011 in the amount of $581,852.26

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2011

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2011

  Received and filed.

10.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July
  2011

  Received and filed.

13.  Community Development Financing Authority (CDFA) Treasurer’s Annual Report
  for Fiscal Year 2010-11 and Annual Review of the CDFA Investment Policy

  (1) Received and filed the accompanying Treasurer’s Annual Report for fiscal year 2010-
  11; and (2) adopted CDFA Resolution 11-02 Approving the Authority’s Investment
  Policy for FY2011-12.

City Council Minutes  3  September 19, 2011
 14.  Annual Weed Abatement Program for Parcels Under One Acre - Year 2011 - Phase
  1 - Round II

  (1) Adopted Resolution 11-59 Declaring that Certain Weeds, Rubbish, Refuse, and Dirt
  on Parcels Under One Acre Constitute Nuisances; Declaring the Intention of the City
  Council to Order the Abatement of Said Nuisances; and Fixing a Time and Place for
  Hearing Protests; (2) instructed the Public Services Department to mail a Notice to
  Destroy Weeds in accordance with Section 39566 of Government Code; and (3)
  instructed the City Clerk to set the Public Hearing for November 7, 2011.

16.  Transfer of Southern California Edison Rule 20A Allocations

  Authorized the City Manager to enter into an agreement with the City of Newport Beach
  to transfer the City's unused Rule 20A allocation of $188,255 within the Southern
  California Edison (SCE) Service Area to the City of Newport Beach in exchange for
  compensation in the amount of $94,127.50.

18.  Fiber Communication and Traffic Controller Upgrade Project, Various Locations
  (CIP 797) — Rebid of Additive Items

  Awarded the construction contract in the amount of $230,588 to Flatiron Electric Group,
  Inc., for the subject project.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

21.  Use of Supplemental Law Enforcement Services Fund

  Emergency Services Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  At the hour of 6:38 p.m., Mayor Leckness opened the public hearing. After hearing no
  requests to speak, Mayor Leckness closed the public hearing.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to (1) approve the
  Use for the Supplemental Law Enforcement Services Fund; and (2) adopt Resolution 11-
  61 Amending the Fiscal Year 2011-12 Police Services Budget to Reduce General Fund
  Revenues and Expenditures and Replace with Supplemental Law Enforcement Services
  Fund Revenue and Expenditures.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Kelley

City Council Minutes  4  September 19, 2011
 OLD BUSINESS

22.  Re-Introduction of Modified City Ordinance Electing to Comply with and
  Participate in the Voluntary Alternative Redevelopment Program Contained In
  Division 24, Part 1.9 of the California Health And Safety Code; Recognition of
  Payment Schedule Pursuant To Part 1.85 of Division 24 of the California Health
  and Safety Code and Agreement to Transfer Tax Increment Pursuant to Part 1.9 of
  Division 24 of The California Health And Safety Code; Acceptance of Transmittal
  of an Initial Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule and an Agreement to
  Transfer Tax Increment

  Special Counsel Celeste Brady presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed her opposition to the proposed action.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to re-introduce and
  conduct first reading of modified City Ordinance 11-291 Electing to Comply With and
  Participate in the Voluntary Alternative Redevelopment Program Contained in Division
  24, Part 1.9 of The California Health And Safety Code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: Kelley

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to adopt CDA
  Resolution 11-13 Adopting the Initial Recognized Payment Schedule Pursuant to Part 1.8
  of Division 24 of the California Health and Safety Code and Approving an Agreement to
  Transfer Tax Increment Between the City and the CDA Pursuant to Part 1.9 of Division
  24 of The California Health And Safety Code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: Kelley

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to adopt Resolution
  11-60 Accepting Transmittal of an Initial Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule and
  Approving an Agreement to Transfer Tax Increment Between the City and the CDA
  Pursuant to Part 1.9 of Division 24 of The California Health And Safety Code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  5  September 19, 2011
   AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: Kelley

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht noted that the August 15, 2011, Minutes did not reflect her
  opposition to the $10 million Enforceable Obligation Payment Schedule (item 31.)

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to approve the
  Minutes for the regular City Council Meetings of August 15, 2011, and September 6,
  2011, as presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Kelley

3.  Check Register dated August 19, 2011 in the amount of $548,126.30

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about payments to GSL Associates and she asked
  what service they provide to the City regarding housing. City Manager Wilberg
  responded that GSL is currently working on the Regional Housing Needs Assessment
  (RHNA) for the next planning period and they also provide support related to the SCAG
  Transportation Committee that Council Member Kelley serves on.

  Motion made by Mayor Leckness, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Kelley

4.  Check Register dated August 26, 2011 in the amount of $2,140,162.32

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she was under the impression that DUI checkpoints
  were fully funded by grants yet the City paid $2,200 for DUI check points. She noted

City Council Minutes  6  September 19, 2011
   that the State legislature has declared that checkpoints have been abused and they are
  looking to narrow the parameters. She stated that she doesn't like DUI checkpoints and
  she feels they are unconstitutional.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Kelley

6.  Quarterly Check Registers and Quarterly Cash Receipts Report - Fourth Quarter
  of FY 2010-11

  Council Member Reardon inquired about cell site payments to ATS Communications.
  City Attorney Curley and Mayor Pro Tem Ury responded that those are lease pass-
  through payments.

  Council Member Reardon asked about the payment to Baja Finistera Condominium
  Association. Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon stated that the City paid the HOA
  for right-of-way associated with the Oso Parkway improvement project.

  Council Member Reardon questioned the bid process for graffiti removal, steam
  cleaning, and painting services. Public Services Manager Jerry Hill outlined the bid
  process for the maintenance contract, one firm's protest regarding a competitors bid, and
  the final decision to award the contract to Bonanza.

  Both Council Member Reardon and Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with
  the City's bidding procedures and expressed an interest in discussing the bid process at a
  future date.

  Motion made by Mayor Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Kelley

8.  Community Development Agency (CDA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2011

City Council Minutes  7  September 19, 2011
   Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with the right-of-way payment from
  Community Development Agency funds when those funds had been suspended. She
  stated that the City Manager acknowledged this to her in an email on August 1, 2011.
  Mr. Wilberg noted that the check for the Mission Viejo Country Club, reflected on this
  Treasurer’s report, was voided and the payment has not been made. He indicated that the
  City will have to use its money to purchase the right-of-way initially, and the City will be
  reimbursed when redevelopment matters are resolved.

  Motion made by Mayor Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Kelley

11.  City Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2010-11 and Annual Review of
  City’s Investment Policy

  Council Member Schlicht asked how the Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF)
  membership affects the value of the portfolio. Director of Administrative Services,
  Cheryl Dyas, stated that it doesn’t have any effect on the City’s membership in LAIF.

  Council Member Schlicht drew attention to the fact that the City’s interest income has
  fallen greatly and she feels the Council should be more fiscally responsible. She also
  asked about the City’s liquidity and cash verses investments. Mrs. Dyas answered that
  staff stays on top of cash flow projections and works very hard to match outflows with
  liquidity.

  Council Member Schlicht and staff discussed the City’s sale of cell site leases and the
  reason for doing so in the past. City Attorney Curley noted that it was an effort to be
  good stewards of the assets when technology was changing and it was not driven by
  panic or any necessity for cash.

  Motion made by Mayor Leckness, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to (1) receive
  and file the accompanying City Treasurer’s Annual Report for fiscal year 2010-11; (2)
  adopt Resolution 11-58 Approving the City’s Investment Policy for FY 2011-12; and (3)
  set the Benchmark Index for FY 2011-12 to be a Government Securities Index comprised
  of 60% three-month Treasury Bills; 25% Treasury and Agency securities with maturities
  greater than one year and up to three years; and 15% Treasury and Agency securities with
  maturities greater than three years and up to five years.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury

City Council Minutes  8  September 19, 2011
   NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Kelley

12.  Community Development Agency (CDA) Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal
  Year 2010-11 and Annual Review of the CDA Investment Policy

  Council Member Schlicht reiterated her comments regarding the City’s general fund
  portfolio that is decreasing while redevelopment funds are increasing.

  Motion made by Mayor Leckness, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to (1) receive and file
  the accompanying Treasurer’s Annual Report for fiscal year 2010-11; and (2) adopt CDA
  Resolution 11-12 approving the City’s Investment Policy for FY 2011-12.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Kelley

15.  Mission Viejo Library Friends Community Room Remodel (CIP 601)

  Director of Library Services Stephanie Tanton presented the staff report.

  Council Member Reardon asked for clarification on the project in terms of drawings, bid
  packages and specifications. Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith
  Rattay noted that the specifications were included in the staff report and the bid
  documents will include technical details and working drawings.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with the cost of the project. Mr. Rattay
  responded that the square foot costs for the community room remodel are far higher than
  that of the average room due to the electronic equipment, the theme, and the highly
  customized features.

  Motion made by Mayor Leckness, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to approve the
  bid specifications and authorize staff to advertise for construction bids.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Kelley

17.  La Paz Roadway and Bridge Widening Improvements (CIP 756/761)

City Council Minutes  9  September 19, 2011
   Council Member Schlicht expressed concern that this is another change order and asked
  why these items were not part of the original budget. Director of Public Works Mark
  Chagnon replied that those items were in the original scope of work however design
  standards have changed since the contract was issued.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to (1) authorize the
  approval of Change Order 3 in the amount of $351,084 to Parsons Transportation Group,
  Inc., for additional design services; and (2) approve an agreement with Moulton Niguel
  Water District to incorporate the design and construction of a reclaimed water line into
  the subject project, subject to any minor revisions required by the City Attorney.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Kelley

16.  Transfer of Southern California Edison Rule 20A Allocations (Revisited)

  Although this item was approved on the Consent Calendar, Council Member Reardon
  asked to revisit the subject so Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon could describe
  Rule 20A projects and funds. Mr. Chagnon stated that the City does not have any
  projects for undergrounding utilities that would qualify for the Rule 20A funds therefore
  staff proposed to sell the City's Rule 20A funds to the City of Newport Beach which has
  qualifying projects. Mission Viejo will realize .50 cents on the dollar rather than losing
  the monies.

19.  Oso Parkway Storm Drain & Water Quality Treatment Improvements (CIP 207)

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she is concerned about the City’s bidding process
  and she recommended giving this contract to the 2nd bidder, rather than the low bidder.
  City Attorney Curley cautioned against doing that without a meaningful basis and he
  reminded the Council that State law and the Municipal Code dictate that the City must
  award the contract to the lowest responsible bidder.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to award the
  construction contract in the amount of $394,122 to PALP, Inc., dba Excel Paving
  Company for the subject project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: Kelley

City Council Minutes  10  September 19, 2011
 20.  Employment Contract for Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services, W.
  Keith Rattay

  By consensus, the City Council continued this item to the next City Council Meeting.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

23.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  In Council Member Kelley’s absence, Mayor Leckness continued this item to the next
  City Council Meeting.

24.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Ury presented the report.

25.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Leckness noted that he had nothing new to report from the San Joaquin Hills TCA.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

26.  FY 2010/11 Budget Amendments and Carryovers and FY 2011/12 Budget
  Adjustments

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented an outline of the unspent FY
  2010/11 funds and higher revenues received as a result of increased property tax and
  sales tax receipts.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 11-62 Amending the FY 2010/11 City Budget for Year-End
  Adjustments in Certain Accounts; and (2) adopt Resolution 11-63 Amending the FY
  2011/12 City Budget to Reflect Final Carryovers from FY 2010/11 and Certain Other
  Adjustments.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Kelley

City Council Minutes  11  September 19, 2011
 City Attorney’s Report

Council Member Schlicht inquired about Vehicle License Fees that the State took from local
agencies and how that affects the City of Mission Viejo. City Manager Wilberg responded that
the battle is still going on in the State legislature and it will affect Mission Viejo to the tune of
$200,000.

Council Member Schlicht asked the City Attorney about a recent court ruling regarding day
laborers and whether or not the City's ordinance is secure. City Attorney Curley responded that
the City's ordinance is still valid.

Council Member Schlicht also asked about the status of the safety concerns at the former Kmart
property. Mr. Wilberg announced that Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson has
been working with the property owner, UDR, on cleanup efforts.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

27.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon outlined her attendance at a recent meeting of the ACC-OC and a
League of Cities Board of Directors meeting. She also attended a Mission Viejo High School
football game where she was pleased to see young Cade Spinello wearing his own football jersey
and his family receiving a generous donation. She also attended a fundraiser as Saddleback
Lanes and an Atria del Sol fundraiser in Aliso Viejo. She reminded her colleagues to continue
praying for Cade Spinello and for Council Member Kelly after the loss of her father.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht expressed her deepest condolences to Trish Kelley and her family.

Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Ury discussed his attendance at a strategic planning session of the Association
of California Cities, Orange County and he noted that he will discuss the strategic planning
points with the Council at a future meeting. He also thanked the Boy Scouts and Girl Scouts as
well as those who planned the 9-11 remembrance ceremony. Mayor Pro Tem Ury expressed his
condolences to Council Member Kelley.

City Council Minutes  12  September 19, 2011
 Mayor Leckness

Mayor Leckness discussed his tour, this afternoon, of the Oso Creek Trail and his attendance at
the recent Inner Coastal cleanup event. He also outlined his discussion with Mission Viejo
Activities Committee member Cathy Allen who recently returned from Joplin, Missouri where
she delivered Mission Viejo's $10,000 donation to the community that was devastated by a
tornado in May of this year. Mayor Leckness closed the meeting with a few details on the life of
Trish Kelley's father, Bernie Thompson.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:31 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Leckness adjourned the meeting in memory of Council Member Kelley’s father, Bernie
Thompson, to Monday, October 3, 2011, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 3, 2011

City Council Minutes  13  September 19, 2011
